67f9 title '(expand half)'; its Approach: 'Registering the name here is inert on its own — nothing stamps it in this story ... The conditional stamp lands separately.' Its ACs cover only classification + write-refusal, none asserts a single-commit tree.

462d Approach: 'the *authoritative* multi-project-bridge stamp is written by the bridge projects set/remove write path — the stamp and the mapping mutation land in the SAME tracker commit ... findings.finding: Parent AC7's atomic single-commit requirement — 'the stamp and mapping mutation land in one tracker commit (asserted on the commit's tree)' — is delivered by NO child in the roster. The parent decomposition scopes this to a 'Store-compat capability stamp' child that changes _store_compat_unit's check-then-act and makes the bridge projects write path write the re-derived stamp + mapping mutation in the SAME tracker commit, but that child is absent: 67f9 is only the 'expand half' (registers multi-project-bridge, tests classification/write-refusal, stamps nothing), 462d writes the stamp only as a level-triggered ensure BACKSTOP explicitly decoupled from the mapping mutation and 'NOT the trigger', and c927 (the bridge projects write path) has no acceptance criterion about writing .store-compat.json at all.
scenarios: A single-project store gains a second project via 'bridge projects set': the mapping mutation must publish atomically with the required_capabilities stamp so a crash leaves neither and no older binary ever observes a multi-project mapping without the guard stamp. No child implements or tests this write path; the backstop ensure runs on a later sweep, leaving a window where the store is multi-project but unstamped.
The parent completion verifier checks AC7's 'asserted on the commit's tree' clause and finds no child delivering it.
findings.suggested_fix: Introduce the missing 'Store-compat capability stamp' child (the contract half of 67f9/462d) that owns _store_compat_unit's re-derive logic and the bridge-projects atomic-commit writer, with a test asserting stamp+mapping land in one tracker commit (tree-level), or extend c927's scope to write the stamp in the same commit as the mapping mutation and assert it.

findings.finding: Dependency/assumption gap: child 462d's design narrative depends on an atomic-commit stamp writer in the 'bridge projects set/remove write path' that no sibling actually builds. 462d states the write path publishes the stamp and mapping mutation in the same commit and positions its own ensure unit merely as a backstop 'for a crash between the write path's two writes' — but c927 (the story that owns the bridge projects write path) delivers no such stamp write, so 462d's stated primary mechanism has no implementer.
scenarios: Implementer of 462d reads 'the write path already stamps atomically' and builds only the backstop, but the write path (c927) never stamped anything, so the only stamping is the level-triggered ensure sweep — contradicting 462d's own claim that the ensure is 'never the primary trigger.'
findings.suggested_fix: Either build the atomic-commit stamp writer in c927/a new child so 462d's backstop framing is accurate, or amend 462d to declare the ensure unit the primary (not backstop) stamp path and drop the 'crash between the write path's two writes' rationale.
